steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression (treated vs control)
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated and control liver samples (3 vs 3, unpaired, single batch)?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald + apeglm shrinkage is the grounded primary method (R-0001, R-0009); lowered count floor (R-0080) and no-length-correction (R-0031, R-0064) follow from the 3' tag-seq library type; edgeR QL as a second method for the low-replicate robustness check follows R-0001/R-0042; the knowledge check flagged reference_level='control' as differing from the sourced default 'explicit' — an explicit control reference level is itself the correct instantiation of that default given the metadata's condition labels, so the choice is kept and stated in the design.

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with >=5 raw counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size), a floor lowered from the standard 10 because this is a 3' tag-seq library where long genes collect proportionally fewer reads. Build the DESeqDataSet from the raw integer count matrix with NO length correction and NO tximport (counts are already gene-level from STAR/featureCounts), design ~condition, with condition releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference. Run DESeq() (median-of-ratios size factors computed internally, Wald test), then lfcShrink() with apeglm on the treated-vs-control coefficient. Extract results() with independent filtering on and alpha=0.05, inspect and report the raw p-value histogram shape before trusting the BH-adjusted values, and report the count-outlier (Cook's distance) NA flags separately from the independent-filtering NAs. As a robustness check, also fit an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (glmQLFit/glmQLFTest) on the same filtered counts and design, and report the intersection of the DESeq2- and edgeR-significant gene sets (padj<0.05) as the high-confidence set, with method-unique genes listed separately. State explicitly that with 3 replicates per group, statistical power is limited: expect to detect only a minority of true DE genes, mostly those with large fold changes, and that a gene absent from the list is not evidence it is unchanged.

steps.description: Map gene symbols in the DESeq2 results table to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db, reporting the share of genes that fail to map or map many-to-one (drop these with a stated count). Rank all tested genes (not just significant ones) by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column) — the chosen ranking metric, stated here per the disputed-metric rule — and run fgsea preranked GSEA against the locally staged MSigDB Hallmark human gene set collection (50 sets), restricting to sets with 15-500 members among the tested genes, with BH adjustment and redundant-set collapsing. Report leading-edge genes for every significant gene set in both collections, and the overlap between DESeq2-based and edgeR-based rankings if both are available.

plan.title: Liver drug-treated vs control 3' tag-seq DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 human liver samples (3 treated, 3 control) profiled by Lexogen QuantSeq FWD 3' tag-seq, quantified as raw gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples) via STAR/featureCounts, single batch, unpaired. Because the library captures one read per transcript's 3' end, gene counts are independent of transcript length and must NOT be length-corrected (no TPM/FPKM, no tximport). The plan follows the grounded DESeq2 workflow: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to confirm the treated/control samples separate and no outlier sample drives variance before any test is fit; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter tuned down for 3'-tag data (>=5 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size) followed by DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization built into the model — no separate normalization step, since normalization for this design lives inside the negative-binomial fit; (3) an explicit two-group design (~condition, reference level = control) with the DESeq2 Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold changes, and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; (4) preranked fgsea enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (staged locally) and, as a documented follow-up given local availability, Reactome, since only 3 vs 3 replicates gives limited power to call many individual genes but may still show coordinated pathway-level shifts; (5) a report step that states the replicate-count power caveat explicitly (3 vs 3 is at the low end — expect few individual DE genes with the strongest effects, absence of a gene from the list is not evidence of no change), gives the required diagnostic plots (MA plot, dispersion plot), a p-value histogram check, and the full reproducibility record (package versions, gene-set collection versions, seeds). Robustness is added via a secondary edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test in the same DE step so the DESeq2 and edgeR gene sets can be intersected and the overlap treated as the higher-confidence call, per the grounded guidance for the low-replicate regime.

raw counts, no length correction, explicit reference level (control)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics and power caveat
